channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald would not say if Sam Darnold (oblique) would start in Week 12.
item.description: Darnold was able to return to practice on Monday ahead of the Seahawks’ Week 12 game against the division rival Niners. Macdonald suggested he wouldn’t make a call on a starting quarterback before Wednesday though. “I think before making any declarations with Sam, we’ll get through Wednesday, see how Wednesday goes,” Macdonald said. “So nothing official yet. He was able to train a little bit here, do some rehab here, he also was able to get away. He’s optimistic, but I think with today’s practice cadence and speed of today, it’s probably wise to wait to make any declarations until we get through Wednesday’s practice.” Drew Lock, the most efficient quarterback in the NFL this season, could get another start if Darnold isn’t quite ready. It’s an excellent matchup against a 49ers defense that profiles as a pass funnel.-Denny Carter

item.title: Treylon Burks caught 2-of-3 targets for 30 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description: While Burks did little in the box score, he drew a defensive pass interference call in the end zone that set up the team’s only touchdown of the game on a Jacory Croskey-Merritt touchdown run on the following play. his three targets finished tied for fourth on the team behind Antonio Williams’ 12, Stefon Diggs’ six, and Chig Okonkwo’s five, leaving Burks in shaky fantasy territory as the team enters the final two months of play.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Stefon Diggs caught 4-of-6 targets for 45 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description: Diggs was shown displaying clear frustration on multiple occasions, the two most glaring of which came on the sideline following a poorly thrown ball from quarterback Jayden Daniels. History would repeat in the second half when Daniels bounced a ball to Diggs in the end zone after escaping to his right, the former of whom had broken free of coverage over the middle of the field. Diggs’ veteran presence will need to persist through the uneven quarterback play if the Commanders are to make a push toward the postseason during the final two months of play, a road that was made that much easier with the walk off win over the Bengals. Up next are the downtrodden Cardinals in Week 12, where Diggs will remain a viable Flex play in fantasy.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Chig Okonkwo caught 4-of-5 targets for 66 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description: The veteran tight end’s five targets finished third on the team behind the 11 of Antonio Williams and six of veteran Stefon Diggs. Okonkwo remains unlikely to return elite volume in the more conservative Washington offense but can continue to return usable fantasy outings as a viable TE2. He’ll push for TE1 status in a plus matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Antonio Williams caught 9-of-11 targets for 122 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals.
item.description: Williams was the top option for quarterback Jayden Daniels throughout, seeing consistent volume throughout. He staked his mark on the game for good with a 42-yard reception to set up the game-winning field goal as time expired, effectively saving the Commanders’ season in the process. After teasing fantasy upside throughout the first half of his rookie season, Williams finally appears to have earned the top role through the air as he enters the final two months of the regular season as a viable WR3 with WR2 upside in fantasy circles. He gets a tantalizing matchup against the Cardinals in Week 12.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Austin Ekeler rushed seven times for 41 yards in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding three yards on two receptions.
item.description: The box score does little to jump off the page but it is notable that Ekeler played over Rachaad White as the primary change of pace option behind Jacory Croskey-Merritt. Whether that was due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week remains to be seen. Either way, the only fantasy-viable back currently on the roster appears to be Croskey-Merritt, leaving both Ekeler and White of little value moving forward.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Jacory Croskey-Merritt rushed 13 times for 54 yards and a touchdown in the Commanders’ Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 23 yards on two receptions.
item.description: Croskey-Merritt immediately returned from injured reserve to handily lead the team in snaps and opportunities, despite veteran Austin Ekeler playing the team’s first series. More interesting was the fact that Rachaad White hardly had a role, with Ekeler serving as the primary change of pace option, something that could be due to White’s presence on the injury report throughout the week. Either way, Croskey-Merritt appears to have a stranglehold on lead duties moving forward, a role that keeps him as a viable RB2 in the immediate future. That holds true for a Week 12 meeting with the Cardinals.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Jayden Daniels completed 23-of-35 passes for 289 yards in the Commanders’ 22-20, Week 11 win over the Bengals, adding 55 yards on six carries.
item.description: Daniels and the Commanders were unable to get anything going offensively while playing through driving rain in the first half, going three-and-out on three of their first four possessions before their lone touchdown drive of the game on their final possessions before the break. Things would change in the second half as Daniels led five consecutive scoring drives, all of which ended in field goals, proving enough to eek out a victory that could have saved the team’s season. The 4-5-1 Commanders remain two games behind the division-leading Giants with two months remaining in the regular season, but a loss to the Bengals would have made a late-season push toward the playoffs almost insurmountable. Daniels and the Commanders now prepare to face the Cardinals on the road in Week 12, where the veteran signal caller will remain an upside QB2.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase caught 5-of-9 targets for 31 yards in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description: The two teams played to a scoreless first frame through driving rain in Maryland, with Chase appearing to come alive on the teams first possession of the second quarter. He would ultimately be locked up by sticky coverage heavily influenced by Washington’s ability to generate consistent pressure, narrowly missing a downfield shot in the second half in triple coverage that could have propelled his fantasy day toward a usable week. Chase’s next opportunity to flourish comes in a Week 12 meeting with the Saints, where his skillset sets up well to take advantage of one of the highest single-high rates in the league.-Mark Garcia

item.title: Tee Higgins caught 2-of-3 targets for 43 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 11 loss to the Commanders.
item.description: Higgins got in the box score with a 31-yard touchdown reception late in the second quarter after the two teams played to a scoreless first frame in driving rain. The Bengals did not alter their typical pass-heavy ways despite the rain throughout the first half, with Higgins seeing modest volume while primarily matched up against Rasul Douglas on the perimeter. Joe Burrow fed the running backs and tight ends a massive 24 targets in the face of unrelenting pressure from the Commanders, a situation likely to correct against the single-high-heavy Saints in Week 12, where Higgins returns to WR2 status in fantasy.-Mark Garcia
